card.name: Words just before 'combination' or 'pair'
card.fires_on: A modifier or pointer word right before an expected 'combination', 'pair' or 'use' noun, such as 'a bad', 'a powerful', 'this' or 'husband and wife'. It also fires inside drug-pair names.

modes.label: Adjective before combination
modes.description: An adjective after 'a' that sets up the noun 'combination' or 'source'.
modes.example: Underactive Thyroid and Heart Failure a<< Bad>> Combination: Study May 22

modes.label: This before concurrent use
modes.description: The word 'this' pointing back to two drugs used together in an interaction passage.
modes.example: Convulsions have been reported with<< this>> concurrent use.

modes.label: Inside drug-pair names
modes.description: Part of a drug or class name in a pairing, where 'interactions' or 'combination' is expected next.
modes.example: The extent to which SSRI-T<<CA>> interactions may pose clinical problems

card.writes: It raises the chance that the next word is 'combination', 'pair' or 'combinations'.
card.plain: It fires when the text is about to say that two things are used or occur together, as in 'this combination'.
